Resolves #8755

LivePreview accepts `language: 'mermaid'` and reuses the existing Mermaid wrapper for editable diagrams. Monaco gets a Mermaid model and basic syntax highlighting; Markdown authors can use a `mermaid live-preview` fence. JavaScript and Markdown retain their existing paths.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium editor → App Worker → SVG, including visible diagram geometry) → L3 required (editable, readable diagram output). No installed-release claim.

## AC Evidence
No structured ACs on #8755. The claimer-owned Contract Ledger and acceptance record cover the explicit language, wrapper lifecycle, Monaco integration and Markdown consumer.

## Deltas from ticket
- Current owners are `src/code/LivePreview.mjs` and the existing component/main addons. Selection stays explicit rather than guessing from source.
- Real browser editing exposed overlapping `mermaid.run()` calls. The addon serializes the library and coalesces obsolete queued requests per exact DOM element; removed, replaced or destroyed owners cannot receive stale output/errors.
- Mermaid measures text in its host. Local Source edits defer diagram construction until Preview is exposed; popped-out previews continue updating. Renderer imports are fenced against later requests, mode changes and teardown.
- The wrapper admits the Mermaid addon in the current target window before dispatching. Moving an existing wrapper to the real Portal child no longer calls an absent namespace; delayed admissions cannot replace newer proxies or revive destroyed owners.
- One source value now drives the editor and renderer, including empty input. The old duplicate source cache is removed.
- The existing Advanced VDOM fixture now explicitly selects `useDomIds: true`, matching its literal-ID oracle. A controlled run reproduced its inherited load-order failure without either new feature spec.

## Test Evidence
- Red-first: the base rejected Mermaid mode and did not extract an editable Mermaid fence. Three controlled library-ordering arms then reproduced overwritten active source, obsolete target work and stale failure painting before the serialization fix.
- Browser geometry control: hidden-host rendering produced a 16×16 SVG with clipped nodes; the same code rerendered visibly produced a 168×152 diagram. The final component spec requires contained nodes and nonzero readable labels on the ordinary editing path.
- Outside CI: `npm run test-e2e -- test/playwright/e2e/rendering/LivePreviewMultiWindow.spec.mjs --grep 'Mermaid Dev' --workers=1 --reporter=line`. The Dev-only case exercises a real Portal popup, native Source typing with editor/worker parity, child SVG updates, close-to-local restoration and zero page errors. This file is excluded by `e2eCiSelection.mjs`; compiled environments were not part of the local run.
- The popup control first failed with `Invalid remote namespace "Neo.main.addon.Mermaid"`; admitting the target window made the same journey render in the child and restore locally. Contained diagram screenshots were inspected in both windows.
- `agent-preflight`: not hosted here; the shared baseline jobs run the applicable checks.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] Smoke the editable fence with the bundled assets in the next published Portal/Docs build.

## Commits
- `c957572958` — editable Mermaid language, Markdown consumer, serial renderer and lifecycle coverage.
- `24a8e23223` — admit the renderer in the destination window and retain the real popup regression.
